text:
The Islanders scored four times on 2.91 expected goals, and the one that mattered most was the least likely. Bo Horvat's snap shot with one second shy of the first intermission, on a power play, carried a 2% chance of going in. It put NYI up 1-0 in a game CHI controlled by volume, 54 shot attempts to 37, and the Islanders never gave back the lead.

By the numbers, this was closer than 4-1 suggests. The simulated replays favored CHI slightly, 53% to 47% for NYI, and the two teams split the expected goals almost evenly through two periods (CHI 1.64, NYI 1.67). Emil Heineman and Anthony Duclair scored 3 minutes and 54 seconds apart in the second, both snap shots from ordinary looks, for a 3-0 lead. Ilya Sorokin did the rest, stopping 22 of 23 and saving 1.45 goals more than the chances against him deserved. Arvid Soderblom allowed three on 18 shots and finished 0.74 goals below expectation.

CHI got one back when Frank Nazar scored on a slap shot at 17:26 of the third, but Horvat answered 61 seconds later on a 65% chance for his second of the night. NYI took the period 1.24 to 0.81 in expected goals, its best stretch. Logan Stanley set up two goals in 23:54, and the Islanders outhit CHI 25 to 15 and blocked 17 shots to CHI's 10.
